state.comment:
When you do read the history of Africa from more fact-based sources, it becomes clear that colonialism was a solely-destructive force which set BACK development on the continent by centuries, it certainly  didn't BRING any.

In a world where colonialism never happened - Africa would likely by the 19th century have been home to 5 large empires - each constrained by too-powerful neighbours on all sides (it was already developing that way. The Egyption empire stretched as far as modern day Lebanon).  Each with their own advantages. The Zulu's had the best military technology and tactics, but the Askaris had the greatest warriors, perhaps in the history of the world.
Forced into this Pax Africana trade among the empires and later with Europe becomes fruitful and well developed. Africa uses it's own resources - and gets the wealth of it. And Africa stays out of the world wars (no reason to join)... emerging unscathed in 1945 as the most powerful economies in the world.
